topicName: Memory Grants and Workspace Memory Tuning
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Memory Grants and Workspace Memory Tuning in SQL Server"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding how SQL Server allocates memory for query execution is critical for high-throughput environments. Workspace memory, often managed via memory grants, directly impacts the performance of blocking, sorting, and hash join operations."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is a Memory Grant?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a query requires memory to execute operations like sort or hash match, it requests a specific amount of memory from the SQL Server Query Optimizer. This request is known as a memory grant. If the grant is too small, the query spills to tempdb, drastically reducing performance. If it is too large, it leads to memory grant starvation, where other queries wait unnecessarily for available workspace memory."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Identifying Memory Grant Issues"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can diagnose memory grant issues by querying dynamic management views (DMVs) such as sys.dm_exec_query_memory_grants. Extended events and execution plan warnings (like spill warnings) are also vital indicators."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"SELECT 
    session_id,
    requested_memory_kb,
    granted_memory_kb,
    used_memory_kb,
    max_used_memory_kb,
    query_cost
FROM sys.dm_exec_query_memory_grants
ORDER BY requested_memory_kb DESC;"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Tuning Strategies"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Update Statistics: Inaccurate cardinality estimates are the primary cause of over-granted or under-granted memory."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Index Tuning: Adding appropriate indexes can eliminate expensive sorts and hash matches, avoiding the need for large memory grants entirely."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parameter Sniffing Mitigation: Ensure queries are not optimized for an outlier parameter value that demands an excessive memory grant."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Resource Governor: Use Resource Governor to cap memory grant percentages for specific workloads or workloads running in lower-priority resource pools."}]
